newsitem.title: USA: Norand settlement wins final court approval.
newsitem.headline: Norand settlement wins final court approval.

text.p: Norand Corp said on Friday that a settlement reached in August of a securities class action lawsuit against the company and some of its officers, was given final approval by a Federal District Court in Cedar Rapids, Iowa on December 19, 1996.

The lawsuit was brought after the company said in September 1995 that it had recorded charges related to accounting irregularities discovered at its Italian subsidiary and that it had incurred an unexpected shortfall in sales in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1995.
Norand had denied any wrongdoing by its officers.
All claims pending against the company and the officers named in the case have been released, Norand said.

Norand said it believes it was in the best interest of the company and its shareholders to settle the charges in order to minimize the expense of defending the lawsuit and the distraction of managers from running the business.

Under the settlement, shareholders who are members of the class certified by the Court will receive $4.5 million in cash and $4.5 million worth of Norand stock, plus interest from October 17, 1996 less attorney fees and other expenses.
The cash portion of the settlement is covered by insurance. Norand has the option to pay $4.5 million in cash instead of issuing the stock.

The $4.8 million charge relating to the portion of the settlement not covered by insurance and additional legal defense costs was announced previously in August, 1996 and reported in the company's fiscal financial statements.
Norand designs, makes and markets mobile computing systems and wireless data communications networks using radio frequency technology.
Shares of Norand closed off 3/8 to 17.
